correctness.rationale: For W=1 0^{g1}1 ...0^{gk}1 with strictly increasing positive gaps, the chosen odd-indexed marker positions and one zero in the final gap attract each factor: any factor containing two ones meets a selected endpoint; single-one factors can be shifted to penultimate/final markers; pure zero factors are covered in the maximum last gap. For even k=2r, r disjoint uniquely occurring consecutive-marker factors plus the final zero-run factor require r+1 hits. For odd k=2r+1, the chain of 2r distinct unique marker-interval factors forces a unique r-point perfect pairing if an (r+1)-attractor existed, while two penultimate-gap one-symbol factors require incompatible choices of the remaining last-gap zero. k=1 handled separately. Independently enumerated 119 gap vectors and 14,114 factor coverages and exactly minimized 52 finite cases; the analytic proof, not finite tests, establishes gamma(W)=ceil(k/2)+1 for all k.
residual_risks: Requires positive strictly increasing gaps and binary markers; neither all permuted gaps nor optimal-attractor multiplicities follows.
